_meta.description: GPU catalog for the VRAM/throughput planner — capacity, bandwidth, dense BF16 compute, and 3-tier hourly pricing. Keyed by slug (t4-16, a100-80, ...), the same convention benchmarks/data.json's GPU half of each key uses. index.html's GPU_TABLE and generate_report.py's GPUS are generated from this file by tools/sync_data.py, between 'GPU_TABLE:BEGIN'/'GPU_TABLE:END' marker comments in each — edit this file, then re-run that script; do not hand-edit the generated blocks. The row schema carries what both engines read plus the structural fields the v1.1 work needs (vendor, devices, form, caps). It is designed to grow — a vendor tag, a per-board device count, a fabric/interconnect tier are all expected to land on this same table in later commits — so a new column is the likely shape of that change, not a new table.

schema.gb: VRAM per card, in GiB. Matches the manufacturer's marketing number, which is already GiB in practice — nvidia-smi reports an '80 GB' H100 as 79.6 GiB, not 80/1e9*2^30 worth of decimal GB.
schema.bw: Memory bandwidth in GB/s, used as the decode roofline's bandwidth term.
schema.hyper: Hyperscaler on-demand price in $/hr per GPU (AWS/GCP/Azure).
schema.spec: Specialized-cloud price in $/hr per GPU (Lambda, CoreWeave, RunPod and similar).
schema.spot: Spot/marketplace price in $/hr per GPU (Vast.ai and similar).
schema.tflops: Dense BF16 tensor-core TFLOPS. NVIDIA datasheets headline the 2:4-structured-sparsity number (e.g. H100 SXM '1,979 teraFLOPS* / *With sparsity'); LLM inference does not use structured sparsity, so this is the dense figure — half the headline number.
schema.name: Display name shown in the GPU dropdown's option label and in generate_report.py's PDF/CLI output, e.g. 'H100 80 GB'.
schema.vendor: Which vendor's performance constants apply: the key looked up in each engine's PERF table (MBU, decode/prefill MFU, observed band). 'nvidia' today; AMD lands its own entry rather than borrowing NVIDIA's.
schema.devices: How many independent accelerator devices one board presents to the runtime. 1 for every card here. Multi-GCD boards — MI250X is one OAM containing two GCDs — are one catalog row with devices:2, because that is how they are bought and priced, and the engine multiplies rather than the catalog duplicating a row.
schema.form: Board form factor: 'sxm', 'pcie' or 'consumer'. Read today as the NVLink gate — only sxm boards here carry it — and the prerequisite for the fabric/domain tier a later commit adds.
schema.caps: Architecture-determined capability flags. caps.fp8 is FP8 tensor-core support: false on Turing (T4) and Ampere (A100), true from Ada and Hopper on.
schema.default: Present and true on exactly one row: the card the tool selects when nothing else is specified. Derived by both engines instead of each hardcoding a slug.
